title.narrative: Sri Lanka ICT Regulatory Capacity Building

description.narrative: This component will build the knowledge of staff on technical aspects of innovations and international best practices regarding regulation. Given the complexity of recent ICT innovations, and of their implications on the existing regulatory systems, it is essential for the TRC to build its knowledge on innovations such as convergence, wireless broadband, and cloud computing. Simultaneously staff should develop the means to learn about future innovations. Understanding the technical aspects of innovations is important in determining regulatory responses. TRC staff should be able to understand the fundamentals of new wireline and wireless technologies, multimedia systems, etc. in order to make informed decisions about regulating them. Further, given that promoting competition and enforcing interconnection arrangements (which includes market definitions and revenue sharing arrangements) are among the basic functions of any regulator, it is important that staff have an understanding of basic economic analysis to be able to judge the impact of new technologies on market structure and economics. Once the technical aspects are understood, the TRC staff should also be familiar with the international best practices regarding the regulation of the ICT sector. For example, it is now international practice to allow market forces and not regulatory fiat to determine choices of technology, services, and business models. TRC staff will thus have to be appraised of such regulatory developments from other countries, and on the latest academic thinking on regulation. This component will include the following technical assistance activities from an international consultant who will: (1) Organize and conduct a three day workshop to train TRC staff on the technical aspects and regulatory implications of ICT innovations; (2) Guide TRC staff in engaging and developing knowledge-sharing relationships with other national telecommunications regulators; (3) Supervise the preparation of a report with TRC staff on international best practices and policy principles; (4) Support short-term training activities through international conferences and workshops; and (5) Assist TRC to institutionalize internal learning and knowledge-sharing mechanisms. The proposed IDF grant will enable the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission (TRC) to develop its knowledge base and implementation capacity, enabling staff to design and implement the second-generation of legal and regulatory reforms in the ICT sector. Improved capacity will allow the TRC to create a legal and regulatory environment that promotes competition and innovation, and supports the spread of advanced ICT, including broadband Internet services, especially in rural areas. The above reforms will enhance the development impact of the ICT sector and support the Government's agenda to develop Sri Lanka into a knowledge economy.
